lines.text: A vague prompt gets a vague answer. Today you learn the formula that makes AI really useful.
Start by giving the AI a role, for example a friendly study coach or a patient maths tutor.
Then say the task clearly, so the AI knows exactly what to make.
Context is the useful background that helps the AI make the answer fit you.
Say your grade, your subjects, your exam dates and how much time you have.
Describe yourself generally, and never give your real name or school.
Format is the shape of the answer you want to get back.
Ask for a table, a numbered list, five bullet points or a short paragraph.
The right format makes the answer much easier to use.
Show a small example of what you want, and the AI will copy the pattern.
Say the tone too, like friendly, simple or encouraging.
The first answer the AI gives you is only a first draft.
Send a follow-up message, for example asking it to make Wednesday lighter or add short breaks.
Keep improving the answer until it really fits your week.
Here is a vague prompt with no details at all.
The answer is true, but it is so general that it does not really help anyone.
Now watch the same request with a role, a clear task, context, a format and a tone.
The answer is a table built around this learner’s real exam days and study time.
Look closely: the AI said the total was ten hours, but the rows do not add up to that.
We send a follow-up asking it to check the sum and to make Saturday lighter.
Always do a quick check of numbers yourself, because AI often makes small maths slips.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
